column1: # The SECOND value an effect probe writes, when the canonical one is what the
# product already does without the key.
# WHY THIS FILE AND NOT `forms.tsv`. That table asks about the FORM of a value
# and one magnitude per form is enough for it, so it fixes exactly one — and it
# is frozen. Axes B and E ask a different question: whether a key still carries
# ITS OWN EFFECT beside a neighbour. A write indistinguishable from the key
# being omitted answers that question vacuously, whatever the merge did. The
# same reasoning already produced `composition-magnitudes.tsv` for axis C, and
# this file is its sibling for the two axes that compare against an omitted
# side.
# The canonical `bool` write is `true`, and `true` is what almost every
# `*.enabled` key in this tree already is. Measured on the frozen half: of the
# 117 pair sides that write the key `enabled`, 116 changed the object when the
# stand wrote an int at them and 0 did once the repaired generator wrote the
# canonical `true`.
# HOW THE VALUE IS CHOSEN, AND WHAT IS NOT ALLOWED TO CHOOSE IT. The stand does
# not read a default off a key's spelling — a suffix heuristic is the very
# thing this round removes from the product. It OBSERVES: the `omitted` side is
# already taken, so "this write is what the product does anyway" is a
# measurement, and the alternate below is tried only after that measurement
# says so. A key where neither the canonical write nor its alternate can be
# told from the omitted one is read NOT OBSERVABLE by the classifier; it is
# never written with a third value chosen to win.
# THREE SELECTORS, TWO QUESTIONS.
# The first two answer "what SECOND value to write instead of the canonical
# one". The third answers a different question — "what value to write for
# THIS SIDE" — and is described under ONE MAGNITUDE PER SIDE below.
#   `form`        the alternate magnitude of a whole form, applied through the
#                 same shape match the canonical write goes through, so the
#                 form the shape accepts does not change with the magnitude.
#   `option_leaf` a key whose accepted values are an ENUMERATION the canonical
#                 magnitude is not in. The product's own list is the basis, and
#                 the `why` column names where it stands — this is a
#                 declaration read off the product, not a guess read off the
#                 key's name. Matched on the leaf, exactly as
#                 `axis-a-hits.tsv` is, so one row covers the same key at every
#                 depth it is accepted at.
#   `side_b`      the magnitude the SECOND key of an axis-B pair is written
#                 with, so that two keys contending for one pointer can be
#                 told apart. Axis E does not see it: it is threaded through
#                 `Stand::pairSide()` only.
# A leaf row wins over the form row for its key. A leaf row whose value the
# declared shape refuses is a `LedgerError`, not a silently skipped candidate.
# ONE MAGNITUDE PER SIDE, MANY SPELLINGS.
# When a pair's two keys reach the same pointer — which is what "a top-level
# key beside the level key it reaches" means — writing both sides the same
# value makes `both` equal to whichever side one looks at, and the leaf-wise
# comparison in `Classifier::pair()` reads every side as having survived. That
# is not a blind verdict but a GREEN one: measured on this tree, all 465 axis-B
# cells read COEXISTENCE_OK or MISCOMPOSED and none reads NOT OBSERVABLE.
# Side A keeps the canonical magnitude and side B takes 5519, declared below.
# It is ONE number in every spelling, exactly as 7331 and 9137 are: a shape
# decides which form the value is written in, and a magnitude split across
# forms would put a different value on one side depending on a decision nobody
# reads. `string-nonnumber` is the one form whose canonical is not a number at
# all, so its third value is a third word.
# TWO FORMS GET NO ROW, AND THAT IS THE ANSWER FOR THEM.
# `bool` has two values and one of them is the standing value of most `enabled`
# keys; the `scope` enum has two and `all` is the default. No third value
# exists, so those sides cannot be made distinguishable by any declaration.
# They get no row, `writeForShape()` finds no match in the per-side set and
# answers null, and side B falls back to today's candidates with no special
# case in the code.
# The magnitude 9137 is the same kind of number as `forms.tsv`'s 7331 and axis
# C's 4211/8623: far above every threshold default in this tree, so a write of
# it is distinguishable from the key being omitted, and different from all of
# them, so a value surviving a merge can still be attributed.
